title: Energy Resources
seo_title: Grade 4 Energy Resources Worksheets: Renewable and Nonrenewable Energy and the Environment
standard_text: Obtain and combine information to describe that energy and fuels are derived from natural resources and their uses affect the environment.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on energy resources (NGSS 4-ESS3-1): renewable and nonrenewable resources, fossil fuels, solar, wind and water power, environmental effects and energy data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Our energy comes from natural resources.
key_sub: Renewable resources like sun and wind are replaced quickly. Fossil fuels like coal and oil take millions of years to form.
body_html:
How to think about it

The energy we use comes from natural resources.

  • Renewable resources are replaced naturally in a short time: sunlight, wind, moving water and heat from inside Earth.
  • Nonrenewable resources take millions of years to form: coal, oil and natural gas (fossil fuels) and uranium.

Using any resource affects the environment. Burning fossil fuels pollutes the air and mining damages land. Renewable sources make little pollution, but dams change rivers and wind and solar farms need a lot of land.

Example

Is natural gas renewable or nonrenewable?

It is a fossil fuel.

It took millions of years to form.

Answer: nonrenewable

Example

Name one effect of using wind turbines.

They make no air pollution.

They can harm birds and need lots of land.

Answer: They can harm birds.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking fossil fuels are renewable because there is a lot of them now.
  • Thinking wind or solar energy pollutes the air while working.
  • Thinking renewable energy has no effects at all.

faq.q: What is the difference between renewable and nonrenewable resources?
faq.a: Renewable resources, like sunlight and wind, are replaced naturally in a short time. Nonrenewable resources, like coal and oil, take millions of years to form.

faq.q: How do fossil fuels affect the environment?
faq.a: Burning them pollutes the air, and getting them by mining or drilling can damage land and water.

faq.q: Do renewable energy sources affect the environment?
faq.a: Yes, but usually less. Dams change rivers, and wind and solar farms use a lot of land.
